_README: REAL published OAuth client metadata, captured verbatim from the live URL in
`source_url`. Every other OAuth fixture in this repo is invented locally: the
test writes a redirect_uri into the metadata and then sends that same string
back, so it is self-consistent by construction and cannot detect a gap between
what a client PUBLISHES and what it SENDS. That is exactly the gap that made
every `claude mcp add` a 400 (PR #445): Claude Code declares a PORTLESS
loopback callback and then arrives with an ephemeral port.
RULE: never hand-edit a value here to make a test pass. These are observations,
not knobs. If a value no longer matches the live document, the client moved and
the fix belongs in the server. `npm run check:client-metadata` reports the drift.

clients.label: Visual Studio Code
note: VS Code uses this URL as its client_id whenever a server advertises
client_id_metadata_document_supported, and has no DCR fallback to try
instead. Our CIMD allowlist did not carry https://vscode.dev, so
/authorize answered every VS Code user a bare 400 invalid_client while
apps/marketing/public/agent-setup/vscode.md advertised the path.

observed_requests.label: Claude Code CLI connecting to api.deerdawn.com
observed_requests.reported_by: John, running `claude mcp add` against production
observed_requests.outcome_before_fix: 400 invalid_request: redirect_uri does not match a registered URI
note: The literal query string off the failing authorize URL. Stored verbatim as
evidence; the test rewrites only the api.deerdawn.com origin inside
`resource` to the test issuer, because the audience check is origin-bound
and is not what this fixture is about.

observed_requests.label: Cursor before 3.10 registering by DCR
observed_requests.reported_by: scan 11 connection scanner, from Cursor forum reports
observed_requests.outcome_before_fix: 400 invalid_redirect_uri: redirect_uris must be https (or http loopback) URLs
note: Cursor registers by DCR (it publishes no CIMD document), so the observation is
the /register body, not an /authorize query. The redirect_uris are verbatim from
the Cursor forum threads in `source_urls` (Cursor staff confirm the set).
client_name and the grant/response/auth-method fields are the standard DCR
fields every MCP client sends and are the only non-observed values here; the
test does not depend on them.
Before the 3.10.x loopback rollout the custom-scheme deeplink was Cursor's ONLY
callback, so refusing it left no way to connect at all.

observed_requests.label: A DCR client resending a client_id we issued and then lost
observed_requests.outcome_before_fix: 400 invalid_client: this connector is not registered with DeerDawn. Remove it from your tool and add it again to register a new one.
evidence: distinct_id on these events is mcpcx- + sha256(client_id)[0:32]. Hashing every known metadata URL
matched only VS Code (mcpcx-4dea5324..., fixed by the vscode.dev allowlist on 09-21). The other five
client_ids never emitted connector_registration_requested (instrumented since 2026-08-31) and never
succeeded. One of them (mcpcx-97a63c8c...) was resent 7 times across 09-06, 09-12 and 09-17, three
times inside 47 seconds: a client replaying an id from its own config. That fits a DCR registration
issued before #451 (2026-09-06) made registrations durable, while Redis was their only home (the
Codex loss of 2026-09-05 is the one confirmed instance).
note: OBSERVED: the rejection, its retry cadence, the absence of any registration for the id, and the
loopback host:port Codex sends (127.0.0.1:53046, connector_authorize_requested 2026-09-10).
RECONSTRUCTED: the client_id VALUE, which no event has ever carried (only its hash), and the
callback path. The id below has the one shape this server has issued since 2026-06-02, which is
the only property of it the fix depends on.
